summary: I adopt T1 by reissuing the relation search. The supplied tool ledger is empty, so there are no actual literature returns to interpret and no support for the missing production-relaxation/arrest relation can yet be claimed. E0 reports segmented empty-area fraction, B rising from 0.01381 at 0 h to 0.08918 at 24 h while A is 0.00446 at 24 h. These are image area fractions, not RNA concentrations or direct phase composition; fields are nested within two preparations. Preserve C1 hypothesis H1: xdot=alpha*r(t)-x/tau, where x is an effective dimensionless junction state, r is a reduced production rate (h^-1), tau is relaxation time (h), alpha is dimensionless. Before threshold crossing x>=x_c, qdot=k_n*max(x-x_c,0)-k_d*q; after the first crossing impose qdot=0 as a phenomenological trapping rule. q is only provisionally mapped to segmented area fraction y_area=q+epsilon. At equal integrated production and matched final composition, a pulse may cross x_c and trap q while a slower schedule may not; equilibrated composition-driven demixing predicts schedule-independent convergence. This is conditional on H1 and the uncalibrated observation map.

candidates.target: Delayed emergence and persistence of segmented internal RNA-poor cavities in transcribing RNA droplets, particularly B versus A.
known_relations: E0: t=0 A=0.01487 and B=0.01381; t=24 h A=0.00446 and B=0.08918 mean segmented empty-area fraction.
E0 is an image area fraction and does not measure RNA concentration, free energy, phase composition, network relaxation, or cavity motion.
Seven fields are pooled across two independent preparations; fields, objects, and SEMs do not establish preparation-level replication.
Amplification effects on template/product populations, carryover, and imaging are unresolved.
No broker search or evidence return is present in this input.
hypotheses: H1 (new, explicit, unconfirmed): transcription-driven accumulation of load-bearing RNA junctions can outrun network relaxation, cross a threshold, generate internal solvent-rich domains, and kinetically trap their area.
H2 (alternative): amplification-linked composition or product heterogeneity changes equilibrium phase coexistence; at matched composition after equilibration cavity fraction is schedule-independent.
H3 (alternative): reaction carryover or imaging/segmentation changes explain some or all of the contrast.

gaps.description: Whether production-driven accumulation can outrun relaxation in an associating RNA network and generate then arrest internal solvent-rich domains, under what material and timescale conditions, and with what rate-history dependence. No returned source addresses it yet.
A/B causal attribution among template/product heterogeneity, carryover, and measurement differences is unresolved.
No direct junction-state, relaxation-time, phase-composition, or cavity-trajectory measurement is supplied; observation map is uncalibrated.

variables_units.q: model cavity area fraction, dimensionless [0,1], provisional map
variables_units.y_area: segmented internal dark area / filled droplet area, dimensionless

equations: At first upward crossing x>=x_c impose qdot=0 thereafter; hypothesized arrest rule, not established constitutive physics.
Observation y_area=q+epsilon only under an uncalibrated segmentation-to-state map.

parameters_ranges.tau: positive; exploratory 0.1 to 100 h, not measured
parameters_ranges.k_n: positive; exploratory 0.001 to 1 h^-1, not estimated
parameters_ranges.k_d: nonnegative; exploratory 0 to 1 h^-1, not estimated

candidates.initial_boundary_conditions: x(0)=x0 in [0,1]; q(0) may equal observed area fraction only if the unvalidated mapping holds; r(t)>=0. No spatial boundary, geometry, or total RNA/solvent balance is specified.
candidates.observation_mapping: Only segmented internal dark area divided by filled droplet area is measured. It is not concentration and need not equal material volume fraction. No fit is claimed. Fields do not provide independent preparation-level inference.
alternatives: Equilibrium composition-driven demixing predicts schedule-independent cavity fraction after equilibration at matched composition.
Amplification-related carryover changes transcription or imaging without junction-mediated arrest.
Segmentation or denominator changes alter y_area without equivalent changes in cavity volume.
predictions: At equal integrated production and matched final composition, a pulse crossing x_c predicts trapped q while a slower schedule staying below x_c predicts no new threshold-generated q; the equilibrium alternative predicts convergence after equilibration.
After crossing, reduced r does not promptly erase q under the imposed arrest rule; below threshold q may decay on timescale 1/k_d.
For constant r, x approaches alpha*r*tau; from below threshold crossing requires alpha*r*tau>x_c. Conditional consequence, not an estimate for A or B.
checks: Dimensional: alpha*r and x/tau have units h^-1; qdot terms have units h^-1 since q and x are dimensionless.
Limit: r=0 gives x(t)=x(0)exp(-t/tau); if x(0)<x_c and alpha*r*tau<=x_c at constant rate, there is no upward crossing.
Persistence follows from the imposed post-crossing freeze and is an assumption to test.
No conservation or geometry maps area to volume; compatibility remains unresolved.
E0 is directionally compatible with delayed B area growth but does not measure x or test arrest or schedule dependence.
evidence_conflicts: Initial similarity and later contrast are compatible with H1, H2, H3, or measurement effects; current data cannot distinguish them.
No returned literature or direct state/phase/motion evidence is available in this input.
